findings.title: Secure protection lags behind accepted publication
findings.message: Protection applies only when a publication is accepted. If the secure field is focused and its text is already published, a refused or delayed publication leaves the previous state. In addition, protectedText requires secureClient == clientID. If a secure node has a nonzero client ID that differs from the one the native layer holds when a query arrives, text is exposed until the next accepted publication. Secure state is also not applied when a client first attaches without a publish.
findings.suggestion: Apply secure protection immediately at the point the client becomes active, or fail closed by treating any unpublished/mismatched client as protected.

finding.title: Diagnostic probe still leaks selection geometry for secure text
finding.message: Probe text was masked but the substring is still taken from attributedSubstringForProposedRange. It returns nil under protection, so this is safe only while that protection is present. The ordering relies on the protected flag matching the client. Other diagnostic fields such as selected ranges still reveal the length of the secret.
finding.suggestion: Also mask selection and marked ranges in diagnostic output when protectedText is true.
